A 44-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with fluctuating right upper quadrant abdominal pain.
Her current medications include metformin, glyburide, escitalopram, and psyllium husks.
The patient has a medical history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, depression, anxiety, and irritable bowel syndrome.
On exam, the patient is an obese woman with pain upon palpation of the right upper quadrant.
Her lab values and clinical presentation remain unchanged 24 hours later.
Her temperature is 99.2°F (37.3°C), pulse of 95/min, blood pressure of 135/90 mmHg, respirations of 15/min with 98% oxygen saturation on room air.
The pain was initially a 4/10 in severity but has increased recently to a 6/10 prompting her to come in.
